51072253.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to catalytic domain of human PARP1 after 5 mins by surface plasmon resonance assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Binding affinities were determined by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) using a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare). The catalytic domain of human PARP1 (residues 1-500) was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip via amine coupling. Compounds were diluted in HBS-EP buffer (10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.005% P20) and injected at concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 100 µM at a flow rate of 30 µL/min. Association and dissociation phases were 120 and 180 seconds, respectively. Regeneration was achieved with 10 mM glycine-HCl, pH 2.0. Data were analyzed using Biacore T200 evaluation software with a 1:1 Langmuir binding model. The reported Kd values are the mean of at least two independent experiments.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Figure 2. Overlay of 1UK0 ligand in PARP-1 with benzoxazinone 2a.
